PUBLIC COMMENTS: None

STUDY SESSION:

1.  Public Safety Review and Discussion

  City Manager de Geus introduced the Study Session, thanking Lost Hills Station
  Captain Seetoo and other Sheriff personnel for attending. He mentioned that the
  Study Session was intended to address public safety efforts, recent crime trends,
  and ideas for future public safety strategies.

  City Manager de Geus reported that the City of Westlake Village contracts with the
  Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department (LASO) to provide citywide policing
  services. He stated that Westlake Village spends approximately $3. 7 million
  annually, 26% of the annual budget on public safety related costs as public safety
  is the highest priority for the City Council. LASO is one of the largest police
  departments in the country and contracting with them provides access to many
  services without the accompanying overhead for equipment and facilities.
  Annually, the City purchases minutes for service, which then provides access to
  all other special services as needed (SWAT, K-9 units, forensics, etc.).

  Lost Hills Sheriff's Station is the local station, servicing the cities of Westlake
  Village, Agoura Hills, Hidden Hills, Calabasas, Malibu, and the local portions of
  unincorporated LA County. Deputy City Manager Eskandar is the City's staff
  member assigned to Public Safety and Emergency Services.

  Lost Hills Sheriff's Station Captain Seetoo introduced Sheriff staff members in
  attendance: Lieutenant Roman Foss, Detective Angela Lopez, Sergeant Marcos
  Escalante, Sergeant Brandon Painter and Deputy Brian Knott.

  Captain Seetoo began with reviewing Part 1 Crimes, serious crimes that the
  Federal Government monitors and compares by cities across the nation. Captain
  Seetoo stated that crimes in Westlake Village are down. She reviewed residential
  burglaries, reporting for 2022, there have been ten residential burglaries which
  includes one attempted burglary. Captain Seetoo noted that over 50% of the
  incidents were no-force burglaries, meaning doors or windows were left open or
  unlocked allowing the burglar easy entry into the home. She reminded residents
  to ensure their property is locked when they leave their homes.

  Captain Seetoo reported that Lost Hills Sheriff's Station personnel will be attending
  Homeowner Association Board meetings to discuss crime and crime prevention
  methods. Other efforts included developing a pamphlet on how to protect property,
  reviewing best practices of other police departments to modify the Sheriff's station
  best practices, developing social media posts to inform residents what they can do
  to implement safety measures, and investing in technology to assist with solving
  crimes.
   City Council Study Session Minutes
  City of Westlake Village  September 28, 2022  3

  STUDY SESSION (continued):

  l  Captain Seetoo reviewed three cases and shared how they were solved. All cases
  involved multi-agency partnerships, resulting in increased suspect charges and
  successful arrests.

  Captain Seetoo reviewed Westlake Village calls for service and shared analysis to
  ensure resources are being deployed accurately. This analysis will be provided to
  the City Manager yearly to establish and ascertain any adjustments in services.

  Captain Seetoo discussed how residents can partner with law enforcement for a
  safer community including locking doors and windows, creating a Neighborhood
  Watch Program, calling the Lost Hills Station when a resident sees something
  unusual before posting on social media, investing in smart garage doors, lightbulbs
  and doorbells that allow homeowners to use smartphones to view their home
  remotely and, to turn on lights when away giving the appearance of an occupied
  home, stopping mail delivery when away, and coordinating package pickup with
  neighbors.

  Lastly, Captain Seetoo presented items for City Council consideration as future
  enhancements to assist with crime prevention: automatic license plate reader
  cameras, increasing Volunteers on Patrol, extra Sheriff Patrol units, investing in
  investigative technology for detectives, funding a Regional Crime Analyst for the
  Las Virgenes/Malibu Council of Governments (COG), conducting a Safety
  Symposium and lastly, the five C's (Citizens, City Manager, City Council, Cops and
  Coffee) allowing residents to meet and discuss issues/concerns with City staff,
  elected officials and Sheriffs deputies.

  City Council discussion included: reasons why crime rates were lower during
  COVID, potential criteria for homes chosen for burglaries, appropriate response if
  one confronts a burglar, increasing communication between residents and the
  Sheriffs Department, improving and increasing residential awareness of new
  developments, and ways to make the City safer.

  Sheriff's staff reported that during COVID, residents were home, so burglaries
  I  decreased. There were noted trends for crime at dinnertime is when burglars'
  entry occurs, especially in homes without proper lighting or with doors or windows
  j  unlocked, and without dogs present. The Sheriff stated that if you come home and
  see a burglary in process, leave immediately and call 9-1-1. Many burg la rs also
  enter through the second-floor window.

  Captain Seetoo stated that Sheriff activity reports will become more frequent with
  the City Manager, while working towards_daily reports. She noted that traffic
  enforcement saturation has been deployed in the City to continuously address
  speeding concerns.

STUDY SESSION (continued):

  City Council encouraged Captain Seetoo to share "wins" with residents on a more
  frequent basis. Sharing wins can become a deterrent to stop certain activities, like
  speeding and loud engines. Councilmembers commented that sharing when a
  crime has been solved, reduces residents' anxiety.

  City Manager de Geus thanked Captain Seetoo and the Sheriffs staff for the
  presentation. He reiterated that Westlake is a safe community, but to keep it safe
  takes work, perseverance, commitment, and communication. He commented that
  the City has work ahead related to communication. City Manager de Geus
  expressed appreciation for the increased communication with the Sheriffs
  Department stating that Public Safety is extremely important, and the additional
  communication will assist in the City's efforts. LASO staff are working on a Safety
  Symposium, planning more Coffee with the Cops events, and enhancing the
  Volunteers on Patrol program for which the City received a grant to purchase a
  new vehicle for the Volunteers on Patrol program. Staff will be back with updates
  on this important topic.

ADJOURNMENT:

Meeting adjourned at 5:39 p.m. to the Regular Session scheduled for 6:30 p.m.
